bridge_diagnostic.model: lag-2 relative redistribution ~ past performance S_t + current performance S_t+1 + outcome-interval prior size + colony fixed effect
bridge_diagnostic.interpretation: Past performance retains incremental information about t+1 to t+2 redistribution after measured t+1 performance, current group size and persistent colony identity are included.

ecological_interpretation: Relative reproductive performance has weak but detectable one- to two-year memory, so persistent local-state processes remain viable. Past performance also retains incremental information about later within-island redistribution after measured t+1 performance, outcome-interval group size and persistent colony identity are included. Because measured reproductive performance is an imperfect proxy for any latent environmental state, that bridge coefficient does not by itself prove a separate biological-memory mechanism. The leave-one-island-out diagnostic shows that the one-year performance autocorrelation is spatially heterogeneous: excluding Torgersen nearly removes rho_1, whereas the bridge coefficient remains positive under every single-island exclusion. The defensible conclusion is therefore a mixed history-dependent system in which persistent local state and short-lived demographic information are both viable, while the identity of the process carrying that history remains unresolved.
claim_boundary: Do not claim the persistent local environment has been ruled out.

Do not claim that a significant bridge coefficient proves a distinct biological-memory mechanism; measurement error in current performance or an unmeasured persistent state can leave incremental information in past performance.
Do not interpret the bridge model as causal mediation because S_t+1 is post-t.
Do not infer individual public-information use, prospecting, immigration or breeding dispersal from colony counts alone.
The Torgersen leave-one-out pattern is a prespecified sensitivity showing spatial heterogeneity in performance autocorrelation, not proof that terrain or snow causes that autocorrelation.

Direct discrimination among adult retention, breeding dispersal, prospecting and persistent environmental state requires individual-level movement/resight data and/or colony-specific time-varying environmental measurements.
